card: Prevents descriptor and wallet error messages from echoing raw key material back to callers. Descriptors can contain private keys (WIF, xprv), and when parsing or importing fails, existing error responses quote the input text, risking exposure in application logs, external crash reporters, or shared screenshots. The change removes raw key quoting from parse errors, constrains other echoed arguments to lengths that cannot fit keys, and switches higher-level callers to quote the sanitized public form (desc->ToString()).
evidence: PR description: 'Some descriptor error messages quote the string the caller sent, and a descriptor can hold a private key (a WIF, an xprv). The reply then carries the key into places the request may not go: an application's error log, an error reporter, a screenshot shared for help. Even the first characters of a key give away part of it.'
problem: Descriptor strings provided to RPCs or wallet import endpoints can contain private keys such as WIF keys or xprvs. When parsing or importing fails, error strings currently echo the malformed input back to the caller, risking key material leakage into error logs, monitoring systems, and user bug reports or screenshots.

risk.why: Altered error strings in descriptor and wallet RPCs could break external management tools or client software that match on exact error message text.

scope_notes: Modifies error string formats across descriptor parsing, bip32 utilities, rpc/util, and wallet RPCs. External test suites or integrations parsing exact error message text will see changes.
summary: Stops echoing user-supplied key material and descriptor strings in error messages returned during descriptor parsing and wallet operations. Replaces raw key strings with generic error messages, limits echoed tokens to lengths too short to contain keys, and prints normalized public descriptor strings (via ToString) where a parsed descriptor is available. Updates caller error handling in RPC and wallet code, alongside corresponding unit and functional tests.
